means: The product: the engine, the Mac app and the `silo` command.
A virtual machine that Silo runs. It has macOS or Linux inside.
The long-lived computer where your agents work.
A copy of a computer, or of one of its checkpoints, that then lives its own life.
A computer made from a recipe, and not a copy of another.
A saved moment of a computer.
Put a computer back to a checkpoint.
Remove a fork or a fresh computer. It goes to the bin first.
Where a dropped computer waits for a time before it is removed for good.
Freeze a whole computer: nothing in it runs, nothing crosses its boundary, and nothing is lost. Undone by resume.
End the programs running in a computer. Its disk stays.
Silo's own small program inside a computer.
The edge of a computer. Everything that enters or leaves it passes through parts of Silo that run outside it.
One way through the boundary. None exists by default.
Everything Silo has written down about a computer: its facts and its reports, in the order they came, never changed afterwards.
One thing Silo saw itself, from outside the computer. Written once.
One thing a program inside the computer told Silo. Written once. The agent can interfere with it.
What a classifier, or you, think about facts and reports. It can be wrong, and it says whose it is.
Whatever gives an opinion.
Data you set. It is triggered by a fact, so it is exact.
Data you set. It is triggered by a report or an opinion, so it can be wrong.
What happens to one request waiting at the boundary: it passes.
What happens to one request waiting at the boundary: it waits for your answer.
What happens to one request waiting at the boundary: it is refused.
Said of an action after which a computer can do something it could not just before.
Said of an action that ends or erases something, and that cannot be undone.
Said of an action that is neither granting nor destructive, so a wrong one costs only time.
The request waits at the boundary for the answer.
Nothing waits.
What Silo raises for your attention.
What a hold shows you: a request that waits for your answer.
Claude Code, Codex and the like.
One launch of an agent program, and every process descended from it.
A sequence of turns with one model.
One reply of the model in a conversation.
One thing a turn asked for: a command, a file edit, a search.
What a tool call left behind: processes, file changes, connections.
A text that says how to make a computer.
A command run in a fork or in a fresh computer, with an end.
Said of something that nothing else would bring back if it vanished.
A value a computer can use and cannot read.
A sign-in to a model provider, by subscription or by key.
The core piece of Silo. The app, the command line and every tool only talk to it.
